Change: Read every column as text with keep_default_na=False so the letters NA are not converted to missing.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 1 security recovered versus pandas default load (Nano Labs, ticker NA). 12 columns parsed as text.
Why: Pandas' default missing-value list includes NA. That is a real Nasdaq ticker, not a hole in the file. A later yfinance join would drop Nano Labs for a loader reason, not a market reason.
What_is_lost: Nothing in the file. The default load would have lost the ticker identity on that one row.

Change: Drop the File Creation Time footer from the security table after parsing it.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 1 row dropped from the table (not a security).
Why: Nasdaq documents this last line as a timestamp for freshness, not as a 13th instrument. Leaving it in would put nulls in every other column and break unique-ticker checks.
What_is_lost: The timestamp as a row. It is kept as snapshot_at on every remaining row (decision 3), so the fact of when Nasdaq built the file is not discarded.

Change: Parse 'File Creation Time: 0917202614:03' to 2026-09-17 14:03 and attach that value to every remaining row.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 13253 rows receive the same snapshot timestamp.
Why: A stranger opening only the cleaned CSV still needs to know which day's directory this is. The raw trailer would otherwise exist only in the untouched file.
What_is_lost: Per-row variation in 'as-of' time (there is none: one file, one stamp). Timezone is not labeled in the trailer.

Change: Replace the single-space token with missing (pandas NA).
Rows_or_cells_affected: 7634 cells.
Why: Nasdaq's docs only define Q, G, and S, and only for Nasdaq-listed names. A space is a placeholder for 'not applicable,' which is missingness, not a fourth tier. Treating the space as a level would make 'blank' look like a market.
What_is_lost: The fact that Nasdaq printed a space rather than an empty field. That is formatting, not information about the security.

Change: Replace empty string with missing. Do not fill N (Normal).
Rows_or_cells_affected: 7634 cells (all non-Nasdaq listings).
Why: Empty means the field does not apply because Financial Status is a Nasdaq continued-listing concept. Filling Normal would claim NYSE and Arca names were reviewed under Nasdaq rules.
What_is_lost: Ability to confuse 'not applicable' with 'Normal.' That confusion is what we are refusing to create.

Change: Replace empty string with missing. Do not copy Symbol or NASDAQ Symbol into CQS.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 5619 cells (all Listing Exchange Q).
Why: CQS identifiers belong to the CTA tape. Nasdaq-listed names are UTP. A blank here is structural. Inventing a CQS code would pretend those names are CTA-listed.
What_is_lost: Nothing about the securities. We do not invent CQS tickers.

Change: Strip leading and trailing whitespace.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 74 names had a trailing space; 0 leading. Cells written: 74.
Why: Padding breaks exact-name matches and makes two spellings of Alcoa look different. It is not part of the legal name.
What_is_lost: Original padding characters. Restorable from the raw file.

Change: Collapse runs of two or more internal spaces to a single space.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 185 names.
Why: Double spaces are leftover formatting (e.g. 'Adeia Inc.  - Common Stock'). They would split the same issuer into two strings in a group-by.
What_is_lost: The exact original spacing. No issuer in this file uses a meaningful double space (middle initials still have a single space).

Change: Cast text to pandas nullable integer (Int64).
Rows_or_cells_affected: 13253 rows.
Why: A round lot is a whole number of shares. The float dtype existed only because the trailer null forced pandas to promote the column. Integer matches the meaning and the docs ('up to 6 digits').
What_is_lost: Sub-share precision that was never in the file (100.0 vs 100).

Change: Recode Y→True, N→False as nullable boolean.
Why: The field is a yes/no flag, not a three-letter category. Boolean matches the meaning and makes filters like ~nasdaq_traded read as English.
What_is_lost: The original letters Y and N in the processed table. Mapping is one-to-one and stated here.

Change: Recode Y→True, N→False as nullable boolean.
Why: Same reason as Nasdaq Traded: it is a flag. Keeping 'Y' invites accidental sorts where 'Y' and 'N' are just strings.
What_is_lost: The original letters Y and N in the processed table.

Change: Recode Y→True, N→False as nullable boolean.
Why: Test symbols must be easy to exclude from a tradable universe. A boolean filter is harder to get backwards than string matching on 'Y'.
What_is_lost: The original letters Y and N in the processed table.

Change: Recode Y→True, N→False as nullable boolean.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 13253 rows, all False in this snapshot.
Why: Same flag type as the other Y/N fields, so the four flags share one convention. The column stays even though it does not vary: dropping it would hide that Nasdaq still ships the field.
What_is_lost: The original letters Y and N. No True rows existed to preserve.

Change: Add a decoded venue name. Keep the original code column.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 13253 rows labeled. Codes extra to the published A/N/P/Z/V list: Q=5619, F=7, M=1.
Why: A one-letter code is unreadable in a write-up and hides the documentation gap. Names make the stale docs (NYSE MKT, BATS) and the new TXSE code F visible without changing Nasdaq's code.
What_is_lost: Nothing from the original code column (it is retained). Labels for F and M are ours, sourced from SIP identity, not from the Symbol Directory page.

Change: Add the official Nasdaq tier name for Q/G/S. Leave missing when the code is missing.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 5619 Nasdaq-listed rows labeled; 7634 remain missing.
Why: The letter Q already means Nasdaq as a listing exchange AND Global Select as a tier. A name column stops that collision in later filters.
What_is_lost: Nothing from the code column (retained). Missing stays missing.

Change: Add the official standing label. Do not recode missing to Normal.
Rows_or_cells_affected: 5619 Nasdaq-listed rows labeled; 7634 remain missing.
Why: D/E/H are not self-explanatory, and H is a combination code. Labels let a reader see 'deficient and delinquent' without memorizing the table.
What_is_lost: Nothing from the code column (retained).

Change: Rename to snake_case (spaces removed, flags prefixed with is_ where they are booleans).
Rows_or_cells_affected: 12 original columns renamed; table is now 16 columns including derived fields.
Why: Names with spaces are clumsy in code and in CSV headers. The mapping is one-to-one and listed in this log, so a stranger can map every processed column back to the raw header.
What_is_lost: The original header spelling inside the processed CSV. The raw file still has Nasdaq's headers.
